text:
ajay: heads up — saw a customer report where requests from EU prod were routed to the cheap-gpu tier and then fell back to the hosted-small model. looks like routing headers from the edge sometimes lose region/tier hints.

maria: ugh. do we have a repro? any sample headers?

ajay: pasted a sample (sanitized) below:

```
X-Redwood-Routing: {\n  \"customer_id\": \"cust_23\",\n  \"preferred_tier\": \"reserved\",\n  \"region\": \"eu-west-1\",\n  \"candidate_variants\": [\"redwood-v1-small\", \"redwood-v1-quant\"]\n}
```

ajay: but the decision in the console trace showed `preferred_tier=null` and the router picked cheapest first.

maria: that suggests either the header is being stripped/rewritten by a proxy or our deserialize step is dropping unknown fields. cc @jamie for the console trace UI — would be really helpful to show raw routing headers in the request inspector.

jamie: agreed. current trace pane only shows final model and latency buckets. we can add a collapsed "Routing headers" panel with a small json viewer. low effort.

lucas: also needs telemetry — counters for "header-missing-region", "header-missing-tier", and "fallback-triggered:variant". if we don't track these we'll never find frequency.

maria: yes. and link those counters to the request trace so PMs can click from an anomalous spike into a list of example traces.

ajay: one more wrinkle: quota checks run before routing and can mutate the request (we decrement burst tokens). if quota eviction path returns a different tier we should surface that in the trace as a separate decision node.

jamie: proposal: trace decision graph = [ingress headers] -> [quota check] -> [routing policy eval] -> [model variant selection] -> [fallback sequence]. each node shows inputs, outputs, and small reason string. example: "quota: reserved_unavailable -> fallback_to_hosted".

maria: love that. UX note: keep the decision graph collapsed by default but show breadcrumb summary: e.g. "reserved -> hosted-small (fallback 1 of 2)". add a quick link to "show raw headers" and "download trace for audit".

lucas: for telemetry schema, suggest tagging metrics with `region`, `customer_tier_hint`, `final_tier`, and `fallback_count`. that'll make dashboards easy. also add a sample histogram for "time spent in routing eval" (p50/p95/p99).

ajay: can we also encode the variant fallback chain into the routing header going forward? e.g. add `x-redwood-routing: {..., "fallback_path": ["reserved","hosted-small","degraded-api"]}` so the console can surface what happened without recomputing.

maria: that would be helpful but we need to be careful about header size and PII. store only tier/variant ids and reason codes, not customer identifiers.

ops-bot: deploy: feature/trace-routing-panel promoted to staging by jamie at 2024-12-06T15:07:10Z :rocket:

jamie: pushed the initial UI change to staging. it shows the decision graph and raw headers. asking eng-platform for quick review and a small e2e that simulates missing `preferred_tier`.

lucas: i'll add the telemetry counters in the routing service today and wire them to the infra-metrics dashboard. will also add a fallback_count tag.

maria: next steps: (1) ajay to capture a couple real traces from the customer, (2) jamie to add UI change to review, (3) lucas to add metrics + alerts, (4) product to decide acceptable fallback SLAs.

ajay: captured two traces and uploaded to the shared folder /redwood/internal/traces/1849004321_examples.zip. pointing PMs at it now. :white_check_mark:

jamie: will review traces and refine the UI text for reasons. tight timeline — we should aim for staging test and a quick demo to product on Friday.

maria: thanks team. this should make routing decisions much more observable and reduce "silent" fallbacks. :thumbsup:
